record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.context_brief: Reducing conjugacy to a full group
record.original_question: For a fixed ergodic transformation T0 with full group [T0], does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X, μ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on [T0]? Does this remain true after restricting both sides to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.3. Does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X, µ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on [T0]? Does it when we restrict to ergodic transformations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving bimeasurable bijections of $(X,\mu)$ (modulo null sets), equipped with the weak topology. Fix an ergodic transformation $T_0 \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ and define its full group
$$[T_0] = \{ U \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu) : U(x) \text{ belongs to the } T_0\text{-orbit of } x \text{ for a.e. } x \in X\},$$
which is a Polish group under the uniform metric $d_u(U,V)=\mu(\{x: U(x)\neq V(x)\})$.

Consider the conjugacy equivalence relations
- $\sim_{\mathrm{Aut}}$ on $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$: $S \sim_{\mathrm{Aut}} T$ iff there exists $R \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ with $RSR^{-1} = T$;
- $\sim_{[T_0]}$ on $[T_0]$: $U \sim_{[T_0]} V$ iff there exists $W \in [T_0]$ with $WUW^{-1} = V$.

Question: Does $\sim_{\mathrm{Aut}}$ Borel reduce to $\sim_{[T_0]}$? That is, is there a Borel map $f:\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu) \to [T_0]$ with $S \sim_{\mathrm{Aut}} T \iff f(S) \sim_{[T_0]} f(T)$? Does the analogous Borel reducibility hold when both relations are restricted to ergodic transformations?
artifact.category_tag: Borel equivalence relations in ergodic theory
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint shows that the isomorphism (conjugacy) relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the conjugacy relation induced by the full-group action of an ergodic transformation on itself, answering the question in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Unbalancedness of the conjugacy relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations
status_evidence.snippet: We show that the isomorphism of ergodic measure-preserving transformations is not Borel reducible to the relation induced by the conjugacy action of the full group of an ergodic measure-preserving transformation on itself. This answers a question of Le Maître in the negative.
status_evidence.claim: The Borel reducibility asked for fails; the question is resolved negatively.
